title: Chapter 255: Thank You for Tuning In
html:
After emerging from the woods, Chen Ge dropped the passenger beside the road. The moment Uncle Zhang saw him, he instinctively scrambled backward.

“Uncle Zhang, you should thank this young man properly. If he hadn’t stopped my car and rushed back to save you, that robber would have killed you.”

The other driver stayed beside Uncle Zhang. He did not know what had happened, but when he arrived, he had seen the man pinned to the ground. Remembering what they had been taught in safety training, he naturally assumed he had interrupted a robbery.

“You have no idea what I’ve been through.” Uncle Zhang pointed shakily at Chen Ge and the ‘body’ on the ground, but he had no idea how to explain any of it. The night had thoroughly traumatized him, and Chen Ge suspected that he would need a long rest at home.

“Are you all right?” Still holding the fearsome hammer, Chen Ge retrieved his backpack and shoved the weapon inside.

“Y-Yes.” Uncle Zhang stared at Chen Ge, unable to understand why any normal person would wander around at midnight carrying such an enormous hammer. He knew Chen Ge had saved his life and deserved his gratitude, yet the sight of him was still terrifying.

“Good. Be more careful from now on.” To reassure the two drivers, Chen Ge called Captain Yan and explained the situation within their hearing. As Uncle Zhang listened to the conversation, his opinion of Chen Ge gradually improved. He was an ordinary man who had stumbled into something supernatural, and to him, the police protected innocent people. Since Chen Ge knew the police and had saved his life, he had to be one of the good guys.

Once his guard had lowered, Uncle Zhang thought back over their encounters. Chen Ge had never harmed him during either ride. I must have misunderstood him. He’s probably a plainclothes officer on some special assignment. Wait—did he abandon his mission to save me? That happens all the time on television!

Though Uncle Zhang was an ordinary man, he had a generous heart. He resolved to put in a good word for Chen Ge when the police arrived. Unaware of the man’s thoughts, Chen Ge spoke with the drivers for a while, then asked the second one to take him to the offices of the radio program Ghost Talk.

No. 5 produces the show, and No. 12—Lychee—is tonight’s host. They’ve probably already been in contact.

Once Lychee learned that No. 5 had fallen, she might flee and disappear. To prevent that, Chen Ge decided to deliver her ‘salvation’ immediately.

Whatever your reasons, if you commit the crime, you have to face the consequences.

Chen Ge sent Captain Yan his location and reached his destination in less than twenty minutes.

Thank you for your help tonight. Go back and look after Uncle Zhang. I’ll handle the rest.

After paying the fare, Chen Ge entered the building alone. Radio stations demanded strict acoustic standards; inadequate soundproofing could compromise a broadcast. A large program like Ghost Talk therefore had its own studio buried deep within the building. Avoiding the cameras, Chen Ge paused inside the entrance and tuned in on his phone.

Lychee was still telling her story. Casting herself as the protagonist, she used an unusual approach to explain the strange changes occurring around her. The tale was not especially frightening, but its vivid details sent chills through the audience. The upcoming schedule revealed that Lychee intended to continue the series through the following Tuesday.

She plans to create her own ghost story? Could listening to the broadcast cause something to happen to the audience?

Chen Ge could not fathom what the madwoman was planning. He slipped farther into the offices, unconcerned about being heard while Lychee remained inside the soundproof studio.

There isn’t even a single security guard. No. 5 must have been confident that no one would dare cause trouble here.

Chen Ge understood the reasoning; he had never worried about thieves entering his Haunted House either.

He still locked the doors at night, but only to keep curious civilians from wandering inside, being terrified out of their minds, and causing him unnecessary trouble.

Following a map posted on the second floor, Chen Ge took the elevator to the studio. The rest was simple. He drew Doctor Skull-cracker’s hammer and waited outside the door. Lychee continued recording, unaware that danger stood only a few steps away.

You tell other people’s ghost stories without realizing that you’re about to become part of one yourself.

Hammer in hand, Chen Ge listened to Lychee’s broadcast in the dark corridor. Only a few meters separated them.

…

Lychee described the bizarre events she had experienced in the recording studio. Her story portrayed her as a helpless victim hunting the person who had ruined her life, when in reality, she was the killer.

“That concludes tonight’s show. Thank you for tuning in. Sweet dreams, and good night.” Lychee finished her broadcast at two in the morning. She switched off the equipment and remained in her chair, an unsettling expression replacing her usual composure.

She seemed too immersed in her ghost stories to pull herself free. Silence filled the studio. After a long while, she murmured, “What should I try tonight?”

She chewed her fingers and muttered to herself. This was her true face. When she first joined the station, she had been terrified—a young woman telling ghost stories after midnight, then crossing the silent building alone to return home.

The generous pay had compelled her to continue. Over time, whether through familiarity or sheer exhaustion of fear, the terror faded. But as she lost the ability to feel afraid, her mind began to warp into something unnatural.

She began to imagine herself as the monsters in her stories. She enjoyed hiding in the darkness, where nothing could frighten her.

“There’s still some meat in the refrigerator. Maybe I’ll try a different way of cooking it tonight.”

Lychee’s voice remained as lovely as ever. She lowered her mangled hand, leaving fresh blood glistening on her lips.
